tasks.title: Parts of a path
tasks.statement: Write a function file_info(path) that returns a tuple (file name, name without extension, extension) for a path given as a string. Use pathlib. No disk is needed.
tasks.hint: p = Path(path); return p.name, p.stem, p.suffix.

tasks.title: Joining a path
tasks.statement: Write a function join_path(parts) that joins the list of parts into a path using pathlib and returns it as a STRING.
tasks.hint: str(Path(*parts)): the star unpacks the list into arguments.

tasks.title: Save and load JSON
tasks.statement: Write functions save_json(path, data) and load_json(path): save a dictionary to a file (utf-8, Russian letters without escape codes) and read it back.
tasks.hint: json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False) and json.load(f) inside with open(..., encoding='utf-8').

tasks.title: Sum of a CSV column
tasks.statement: Write a function column_sum(path, column) that returns the sum of the numbers in the column column of a CSV file with a header (the values are integers).

tasks.title: Totals by department
tasks.statement: Write a function sum_by(path, key_col, value_col) that returns a dictionary of the value from key_col to the sum of value_col values, for a CSV with a header (value_col holds integers).

tasks.title: Writing a table
tasks.statement: Write a function write_table(path, header, rows) that writes the header row and then the table rows to a CSV (utf-8, newline=''). The checker then reads and parses the file.

tasks.title: Atomic writing
tasks.statement: Write a function atomic_write(path, text): first write the text to a temporary file next to it (path + '.tmp'), then replace the target file with it via os.replace. No temporary file may remain afterwards.
tasks.hint: tmp = path + '.tmp'; write to tmp; os.replace(tmp, path).

tasks.title: Txt files in a folder
tasks.statement: Write a function list_txt(folder) that returns a sorted list of the NAMES of files with the .txt extension in the folder (no nested folders). Use pathlib.
tasks.hint: sorted(p.name for p in Path(folder).glob('*.txt')): glob without rglob doesn't enter nested folders.
